ARM64Bridge makes 32-bit (armeabi-v7a) Android apps installable and runnable on 64-bit-only devices. It adds a small 64-bit runtime to the APK that runs the app's original 32-bit native code on an emulated ARMv7 CPU (dynarmic JIT) and translates its calls into the 64-bit system.

It can also customize any APK: app name, package name, permissions, screen orientation and more. Patched APKs are signed with a key created on this device.
